# LegatorOCR v0.2.0-pre.26 (pre-release)

Changes since pre.25. Written and tested by the author's assistant on one Linux machine; **nothing was tried on Windows, macOS or arm64**.

**New (command line only, not in the window yet)**
- `--duplex-adf`: a stack scanned on a one-side-at-a-time feeder (all fronts, then all backs in reverse) is put in reading order. Needs an even page count.
- `--pages 1-10,15,20-` keeps only those input pages; `--reverse` flips the order.
- `--dry-run` lists the pages in the order they would be processed and the files that would be written, then stops.
- `--find-replace FILE`: your own `wrong => right` corrections (whole words, applied in file order) for the .txt and .docx text, after `--clean-text`. The PDF text layer, hOCR and JSON keep the raw words.
- **The guide PDF is rewritten for this edition** (28 pages): new sections for the options above, `--clean-text`/`--cedilla`/`--drop-running-heads`, `--accurate` and old spelling, with terminal screenshots of real runs on test pages.

**Verified**: unit tests (range parser, duplex order, rules) and CLI tests (`tests/page_selection.rs`); six synthetic pages through the real binary.
**Not verified**: a real feeder scanner; the options inside the window; Windows, macOS, arm64.

**Known limits (unchanged)**: OCR can misread characters such as `@`; a table without ruled lines is found as two tables; the display title of a page with a halftone panel is lost; the rotation behaviour seen on Windows 11 is unconfirmed.
